groups.title: Comparison: which is bigger, and how do they rank?
Shift and swing: what moved, and which way?
Change over time: how has it moved?
Composition: what is it made of?
Distribution and density: how are the values spread?
Correlation: do two things move together?
Uncertainty and estimates: how sure is it?
Proportion and overlap: how much, and how do groups overlap?
Gauges and indicators: where does it stand now?
Behavior: how do people move through a process?
Structure: who decides, and how does it work?
Relationships: who is connected to whom?
Tables and plain words: where does a reader look things up, and when do words answer faster?
Infographics: how does it work, in one look?

chapter_rules.subject: Start from the reader's question, then choose the form
Build every chart in one anatomy: evidence label and grade line, title, reading guide, measure line, chart, notes, source line and table
Label the data directly, and use a key only when labels cannot fit
Start bars and columns at zero, keep one scale per axis, and size circles by area
Give each color a job: sequential, diverging pair B, the four-ink groups, or magnitude
Spend the view's one red on the point the title names
Draw parties in neutral inks with each party named on its mark, never in red and blue
Past four groups, split into small multiples or set one group in ink against gray
Show the publisher's uncertainty, and rank only past the margin of error
Give charts shown together one window with its reason, and never split a period at an inauguration
Mark a gap, a break in a series or a preliminary value in the drawing
Redraw for the phone only when the form must change, with the same data and finding
Carry every chart's table as live text, and publish a still image first
Make every export from the kit, never by hand
